Analysis. It is unlikely that an increase in the number of diesels will occur in the short time frame under consideration and hence, this effect is not discussed in the EIS. However, they will be for future AFES's. Close coordination between NHTSA and EPA has been maintained and this problem is being examined. There is disagreement on the issue of whether the recalibration of spark ignition internal combustion engines will result in increased particulate emissions. However, it is generally accepted that the addition of diesel engines in the automobile fleet will result in increased particulate emissions. EPA is studying both the level of particulate emissions from automotive sources, the level of particulate emissions in the atmosphere, and the resulting health hazard. EPA has stated they will promulgate a rule on particulate emissions if they are found to present a health hazard.
